heading: Writing on AI, systems and communities
intro: I write about building practical AI on a budget, data sovereignty, developer communities and Zimbabwe's technology scene, mostly from projects I am working on.

featured.title: Solving AI: Borrowing from Biomimicry and Society
featured.summary: How designing a multi-persona AI automation system led me to borrow from nature, human onboarding, and workplace access control — and what that means for building resilient AI on a budget.
excerpt: I wonder who holds the most patents in this world, and how they would compare to God. Every time we face a hard problem, the best answers seem to come from studying nature. From aerodynamics to architecture — and now to AI. We even have a word for it: biomimicry.

One day I sat down writing system instructions for an AI prompt destined to be part of Fung.ai. The goal was enterprise-wide automation: defining roles, permissions, tone, and context for every job the system would handle. After the third role, I had had enough. The file was bloating, the logic was tangled, and there had to be a better way.
